items.learningObjective: Separate caller capabilities when two workflows share identity reads but only one may change an assignment, while keeping storage replaceable.
items.decisiveFact: Inspection must not receive an assignment-change operation; swap may change assignment; storage implementation may change independently.
items.nearestAlternative: Give both clients the same interface and hide the write button only in the inspection UI.
items.changedCondition: The scenario now states which client must lack the write capability, making client-specific operation contracts necessary rather than merely recommending a named API.
items.identityReason: The old item was a generic owner slogan. This replacement asks which operations each of two specified clients may call while the persistence adapter remains replaceable.

items.learningObjective: Keep consent checking and summary construction at the dispatch boundary while separating the desk’s submit capability from audit history access.
items.decisiveFact: Only the dispatch boundary may read the consent ledger, check active consent, and build the specialist summary; the desk must not read or construct those values, while audit can read history only.
items.nearestAlternative: Expose the full Referral object, including its consent records, to both clients.
items.changedCondition: The prompt now states that the desk cannot read consent or build the summary; those capabilities belong to the dispatch boundary, while audit remains unable to dispatch.
items.identityReason: The old key was a generic owner maxim; this item now tests a case-specific public contract and its observable outcome, so the primary learner decision and option meanings change.

items.nearestAlternative: Expose status and approver fields so the queue can mark the exception Approved after checking its own checklist.

items.learningObjective: Choose a stable public data projection that decouples clients from persistence fields and row layout.
items.decisiveFact: Clients need only the pass ID, displayed zone, and expiry; the row layout will change and clients must not access persistence fields.
items.nearestAlternative: Return the current PassRow and document its column names for clients.

items.identityReason: The new primary decision is a stable projection versus exposing a persistence record/shape; it no longer tests the accepted annotation-replacement outcome.

items.learningObjective: Keep a resource screen’s access query separate from grant-management authority, including the explicit prohibition on extending expiry.

items.learningObjective: The operation must bind the signer’s confirmation to a specific immutable revision and report mismatch without sealing. The caller should not manipulate revision bytes or storage.

items.nearestAlternative: Expose document bytes to the screen and let it calculate and persist the seal digest.

items.learningObjective: Represent distinct payout statuses and their case-specific reference in a read-only lookup result without giving an observer transfer authority.
items.decisiveFact: The screen must distinguish Pending, Rejected, and Released with a payout reference; a separate service owns transfer initiation.
items.nearestAlternative: Return only IsReleased(requestId), which collapses Pending and Rejected and omits the payout reference.
items.changedCondition: This replacement asks how a read result preserves three states and one state-specific payload, rather than how a stable-key retry recognizes an existing payout.
items.identityReason: The learner now designs an observation result for a reconciliation screen: preserve distinct outcomes and the release reference. The accepted N01 payout item instead decides what a repeated command returns after a payout already exists.

items.learningObjective: Use a common polymorphic operation to process a mixed collection of extension-defined elements while preserving caller-owned sequence order.
items.decisiveFact: New CanvasElement kinds can be installed without editing the renderer, and the renderer must preserve the incoming order.

items.identityReason: This replacement changes the learner decision from a completed-match rejection contract to polymorphic dispatch across extension-defined shapes; all answer choices express new meanings.
